    AI Overview
    Russia, officially the Russian Federation, is the world's largest country by landmass, located across Eastern Europe and Northern Asia. Its capital is Moscow, the currency is the Russian ruble, and the official language is Russian. The culture is deeply rooted in literature, ballet, and classical music, influenced by Orthodox Christianity. 
    Key Facts About Russia 
    • Capital: Moscow.
    • Official Language: Russian.
    • Currency: Russian Ruble (
      RUBRUB
      ).
    • Major Religions: Russian Orthodox (15-20%), with significant Muslim (10-15%) and non-practicing/non-believer populations. 
    Culture and Traditions 
    • Cultural Focus: Known worldwide for literature (Tolstoy, Dostoevsky), composers (Tchaikovsky), and ballet.
    • Family: Family is very important, with common traditions including gathering together to talk, often in the kitchen.
    • Food & Souvenirs: Famous for borscht, pelmeni, vodka, caviar, and Matryoshka dolls.
    • Nature & Travel: Features diverse landscapes, including Lake Baikal, the Caucasus mountains, and the Kamchatka volcanoes. 
    Society and People 
    • Population: Over 120 ethnic groups live in Russia, with roughly 80% tracing their ancestry to the Slavs.
    • Activities: Soccer, hockey, chess, and skiing are very popular.
    • History: The state began to take shape from East Slavic tribes, with a long history of expansion, including the imperial era, the Soviet period, and the modern Federation.

    AI Overview
    Russian history began with the 9th-century Kievan Rus', followed by Mongol rule (13th-15th centuries) and the rise of the Tsardom of Russia. Peter the Great modernized Russia into a massive Empire (1721-1917). After 1917 revolutions, it became the Soviet Union, a superpower until its 1991 collapse, leading to the modern Russian Federation. 
    Key Periods in Russian History:
    • Kievan Rus (9th–13th Centuries):
      Eastern Slavic tribes were united by Vikings in the 9th century, with Kiev as a major center. Prince Vladimir adopted Orthodox Christianity in 988, cementing cultural ties to Byzantium. 
    • Mongol Invasion & Rise of Moscow (13th–16th Centuries):
      The Mongols (Golden Horde) conquered Kievan Rus in the 13th century, resulting in centuries of dependency. Moscow gradually grew in strength, eventually ending Tatar rule under Ivan III (Ivan the Great) in 1480. 
    • Tsardom and Empire (1547–1917):
      Ivan IV (Ivan the Terrible) became the first crowned Tsar in 1547. Peter the Great (1682–1725) and Catherine the Great (1762–1796) transformed Russia into a major European power, expanding territory into Siberia and toward the Black Sea. 
    • Revolution and Soviet Union (1917–1991):
      Imperial rule collapsed during WWI. The 1917 October Revolution brought Vladimir Lenin and the Communists to power. Following a civil war, the Soviet Union (USSR) was formed in 1922, expanding under Stalin into a global superpower after World War II. 
    • Modern Russia (1991–Present):
      After the USSR's collapse in 1991, Russia became an independent state led first by Boris Yeltsin. Vladimir Putin has served as president or prime minister since 2000, overseeing a resurgence of Russian influence and increased tensions with the West, culminating in the 2022 invasion of Ukraine. 
    Significant Historical Events: 
    • 1237-1240: Mongol conquest by Batu Khan.
    • 1812: Napoleon's failed invasion of Russia.
    • 1861: Emancipation of the serfs by Alexander II.
    • 1917: Bolshevik revolution, leading to the murder of the Romanov family.
    • 1941-1945: Great Patriotic War (WWII), resulting in massive losses but victory.
    • 1991: Dissolution of the Soviet Union.
    • 2014: Annexation of Crimea.

      AI Overview
      Moscow is the capital city of Russia. Located on the Moskva River in western Russia, it is the country's most populous city (over 13 million residents), as well as its political, economic, cultural, and scientific center. It is also home to the Kremlin and Red Square, the nation's symbolic heart. 
      Key details about Moscow: 
      • Location: Western Russia, on the Moskva River.
      • Role: Political center of the Russian Federation.
      • Significance: Major cultural, educational, and economic hub.
      • Landmarks: The Kremlin, Saint Basil's Cathedral, and Red Square.
      • Population: Over 13 million residents in the city limits.
